description:
## Why

The harness is only as good as the corpus it can ingest. Two tier-1+2 shapes need first-class loaders.

## What

In `pkix-difftest/src/corpus/`:

1. `mod.rs` — public trait `Corpus`:
   ```rust
   pub trait Corpus {
       /// Iterator of (name, expected_verdict_opt, chain).
       fn iter(&self) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = io::Result<(String, Option<Verdict>, Chain)>>>;
   }
   ```
   `expected_verdict_opt` is `Some` for corpora that have ground truth (PKITS `ShouldValidate`), `None` for in-the-wild corpora.

2. `pkits.rs` — reads `pkits/vectors.json`, resolves cert filenames against `pkits/certs/`, returns chains in the order `CertPath` lists (root-first per RFC 5280). Sets `expected_verdict_opt` from `ShouldValidate`.

3. `pem_tree.rs` — walks a directory looking for `chain.pem` files (or files matching a glob). Each chain.pem is concatenated PEM. Auto-detects ordering. `expected_verdict_opt = None`.

4. `pem_multi.rs` — single chain from CLI args (multiple files: leaf, intermediates..., root). Used for ad-hoc debugging.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Corpus` trait implementations for PKITS, pem_tree, pem_multi.
- [ ] PKITS loader: 249 chains enumerated, every `CertPath` entry resolves to a real cert file.
- [ ] PEM-tree loader: handles concatenated PEM, ignores non-cert blocks (e.g., embedded key blobs), errors clearly on malformed input.
- [ ] Auto-detect ordering test: a leaf-first chain.pem and a root-first chain.pem produce the same `Chain` once normalised.
- [ ] No silent skipping of corpus entries — every entry produces either a chain or an `io::Error` (visible in the report).

## Out of scope

- Tier 3 (CT log scrape) — separate bead.
- Tier 4 (hand-curated quirks set) — populated as Tier 2 surfaces them.
- Per-corpus expected error categories (e.g., 'this should fail with reason X'). v1 only checks Pass/Fail.
